title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the bookkeeping, begun on p. 672, of a family of profinite groups attached to a pair (rho, sigma). These are presumably the order-2 and order-3 generators coming from the action on the profinite free group / profinite PSL2(Z). The groups belong to Grothendieck's study of the 'équation des lacets', i.e. the relations that cut out a Grothendieck–Teichmüller type subgroup of the outer automorphisms of the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}.

The ingredients from the previous page are:
- normalizer-type groups N_rho, N_sigma;
- a group Z_{rho,sigma};
- an 'environment' group G_{rho,sigma};
- a small group gamma_{rho,sigma} over which everything is fibred;
- Gamma_{rho,sigma} = N_rho x_gamma N_sigma and M_{rho,sigma} = N_rho x_gamma N_sigma x_gamma G_{rho,sigma};
- 'S_0' variants obtained by an extra fibre product with Z_{rho,sigma}.

Each group has a 'starred' (decorated) version, written with a superscript that looks like a G with an arrow; the machine transcription renders it as natural. In the decorated versions, G is replaced by G^dec and the unrestricted group (G-hat^+, read here as GT-hat^+) by GT-hat^dec. The latter is presumably the subgroup defined by the loop equation(s).

Formulas (85)-(87) re-express the S_0 variants as base changes:
- (85): S_0 M ≅ M x_gamma Z, and likewise for the decorated M.
- (86): S_0 Gamma ≅ Gamma x_gamma Z.
- (87): S_0 M ≅ M x_Gamma S_0 Gamma, and likewise for the decorated M.
All three follow formally from associativity and commutativity of fibre products over gamma, using the projections M -> Gamma -> gamma. On the second line of (85) Grothendieck writes Z-bar rather than Z; this is probably a notational variant or slip.

In the Remark he says this 'digestion de groupes' gives him a bit of seasickness ('le mal de mer'). He is not sure the S_0 variants will be very useful.

What remains is the compatibility between the invariants in the decorated sense and the undecorated ones in M and M^dec. The decorated subgroups are normal ('invariant') in the undecorated ones: M^dec in M and G^dec in G. There are isomorphisms (88):
GT-hat^+ / GT-hat^dec ≅ G_{rho,sigma} / G^dec_{rho,sigma} ≅ M_{rho,sigma} / M^dec_{rho,sigma}.
The second isomorphism is immediate, because M and M^dec share the same N_rho and N_sigma factors and differ only in the G-factor.

The large groups G and M are described as convenient 'fourre-touts' (catch-alls). They let the rho, sigma actions of the decorated groups be seen as induced (restricted) from actions of the ambient 'environment' groups G and M. This is the start of p. 674, which then introduces lifts tau' and fixed-point sets of involutions.

Purpose: organisational. It sets up a uniform framework of ambient groups and normal subgroups so that actions and fixed-point (tau-invariant) sets for the GT-like subgroup can be read off from larger, easier groups.
errors: Second line of (85) has Z-bar instead of Z, inconsistent with (77) and (86); likely a notational slip or an unexplained variant.

The image seems to read 'M_{rho,sigma} est invariant dans M^dec_{rho,sigma}', with 'précisément G^dec dans G' added below. The quotient M/M^dec in (88) requires the reverse: M^dec normal in M. This is presumably a slip of the pen, or the inserted 'précisément' line restores the right order.
Some exact sequences on p. 672 that these formulas rely on are left incomplete (missing '->1', crossed-out terms); this page does not repair them.

ideas.what: Expressing auxiliary 'S_0' groups as fibre products (base changes over gamma or over Gamma) of the basic groups M, Gamma with Z
ideas.modern_name: Fibre products of profinite groups over a common quotient

ideas.what: Decorated subgroups (GT-hat^dec, G^dec, M^dec) are normal in ambient groups (GT-hat^+, G, M), with all quotients canonically isomorphic, eq. (88)
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type subgroup with an ambient automorphism group via normal subgroups with isomorphic quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT-hat: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991); refinements by Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura and others
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) discusses Galois actions on profinite fundamental groupoids but not, to my knowledge, this specific bookkeeping

ideas.what: Using large 'fourre-tout' ambient groups so that actions of the restricted groups are induced by actions of the ambient ones
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of actions from an ambient automorphism group

deep.surprise_reason: The page is internal bookkeeping: formal fibre-product identities and a formal quotient isomorphism, with Grothendieck himself doubting their usefulness. It belongs to his unpublished pre-Drinfeld work on GT-like groups, whose existence is broadly known, but this page holds no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: The superscript transcribed as 'natural' (♮) looks in the image like a G with an arrow (the next page's transcription renders it as G). It denotes the decorated, loop-equation-constrained versions.
Remark opening: should read roughly 'Cette digestion de groupes donne un peu le mal de mer. Je ne suis pas sûr que les variantes S_0 (S_0 M, S_0 M^dec, S_0 Γ) soient très utiles.'
'So' should be 'S_0' (S with subscript 0), as on p. 672.
Last lines: 'le rôle de fourre-touts commodes pour nous permettre de considérer les actions ρ, σ de G^dec, M^dec comme induites par des actions ... des groupes [environnements G, M]'.
The '\n' and 'atural' fragments in the machine transcription are broken LaTeX escapes for line breaks and the superscript.
